name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 325 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / LAND NEAR THE MISSION OF SAN JUAN BAUTISTA GRANT / MANUEL LARIOS CLAIMANT'; PDF p3 transcript title 'for the place named "Land near the Mission of San Juan Bautista"'. Register's 'Unnamed grant (SD 325)' is a placeholder; the file does supply a designation, and witnesses call the tract 'the Rancho of Don Manuel Larios ... after, it was known as San Antonio' (Ramon Anzar, PDF p17 = 325 SD p.13) and 'it was called San Antonio' (Claudio Vasquez, PDF p16 = 325 SD p.12)

year.evidence: PDF p83 (325 SD page 83), District Court decree: 'the original grant from Jose Castro Prefect to the present claimant dated May 4th 1839'; same date in the confirmation decree PDF p85 (325 SD p.75) 'a Document bearing date May 4th 1839'; petition PDF p9 (325 SD p.6) 'granted to the claimant on the 4th day of May in the year 1839'

governor.evidence: The concession instrument was NOT signed by the governor. District Court decree, PDF p85 (325 SD page 75): 'the same which was granted to him by Jose Castro, Prefect of the first District by order of the Governor by a Document bearing date May 4th 1839'. Jose Castro's own deposition, PDF p13 (325 SD p.9): 'In the Month of May 1839 I held the Office of Prefect of the First District of California... The paper was signed by me as Prefect', and PDF p15 (325 SD p.11) 'Whose hand writing is the body of the before mentioned grant. Answer. It is in my hand writing.' The authorizing governor is named at PDF p9 (325 SD p.6): 'pursuant to an order of that effect given by Don Juan B. Alvarado Constitutional Governor of said Department', corroborated by J. M. Aguilar, PDF p23 (325 SD p.19): 'I saw an Order in writing signed by Governor Juan B Alvarado, in which Order Jose Castro, the prefect was directed to give the possession of the said land to Manuel Larios.' Register's 'Alvarado' names the right administration and the ordering authority, but the granting officer of record is Jose Castro, Prefect of the 1st District

grantee.evidence: PDF p13 (325 SD p.9) Jose Castro: 'A paper is now shown me purporting to be a grant of ownership or possession to Manuel Larios dated May 4 1839 & which is hereto attached & marked H.H. No. 1'; District Court decree PDF p85 confirms 'to the said Manuel Larios'. Here claimant and grantee are the same man, so the usual claimant-for-grantee error does not arise

corrections.governor: Granting officer per the decree (PDF p85): 'Jose Castro, Prefect of the first District by order of the Governor'; Governor = Juan B. Alvarado, who signed the authorizing order (PDF p9, p23). Register's bare 'Alvarado' omits that the instrument is a prefectural grant.

Por cuanto los Ciudadanos Franco y Pedro Lopez han pretendido... he venido en concederles el terreno mencionado declarandoles la propiedad de el por las presentes letras'; English at PDF p26 (52 SD p.21). Jimeno / Jose L. Fernandez Srio Into' - and the claimants' original paper (PDF p186, 52 SD p.173) is issued by 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin primer Vocal de la Excma Junta del Departamento de las Californias en ejercicio del Gobierno del mismo'

Lopez one half (7 May 1851), Triunfo & wife -> Alexander & Mellus one half (31 Aug 1851), F. R. Lopez -> Agustin Olvera one fourth (29 Sept 1851) - petition PDF p9-10 (52 SD pp.4-5)

Final decree, PDF p190 (52 SD p.178), December Term 1856, Isaac S. K. Ogier U.S. Dist. Judge: 'the order granting an appeal to the Supreme Court heretofore made in this cause be and the same is hereby Vacated. And that the Claimant have leave to proceed under the decree of this Court heretofore rendered in this Cause as under a final decree.' Register's 'Confirmed' is right; Hoffman-1862 'confirmed' agrees

corrections.grantee: Francisco Lopez and Pedro Lopez (grant of 1840). Alexander and Mellus are the 1852 claimants, remote purchasers through Miguel Triunfo.

notes: 175MB / 190 PDF images; stated 178 pages. Hoffman's 'Pedro Lopez et al.' agrees with the case file against the register - this is the dominant claimant-for-grantee error. TWO title papers are in the file and they do not have the same date or the same signer: the Surveyor-General's certified archive expediente (52 SD pp.9-16, certified by Saml D. King 6 Sept 1852, PDF p21-22) carries a titulo in the name of Juan B. Alvarado dated 5 Dec 1840, while the claimants' original document H.H. No. 1 (52 SD pp.173-175) is issued by Manuel Jimeno Casarin as acting governor and dated 7 Nov 1840 - the date Abel Stearns gave in his deposition (PDF p11, 52 SD p.6: 'a grant to Francisco & Pedro Lopez dated Nov 7th 1840 & a testimonial of judicial possession attached dated in February 1841'). The wrappers at 52 SD pp.10-11 show TWO 1840 expedientes, one for Tujunga and one for 'un sitio contiguo a Tojunga', which is the likeliest explanation. Either way the year (1840) and the grantees (the Lopez brothers) are the same in both.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 228 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / LOS TULARCITOS GRANT / THE HEIRS OF JOSE HIGUERA CLAIMANT'; PDF p5 transcript 'for the place named "Los Tularcitos"'; decree of confirmation PDF p63 (228 ND p.49) 'is known by the name of Los Tularcitos'. The register's parenthetical '(Higuera)' matches the file's grantee

year.evidence: Board's opinion, PDF p59 (228 ND p.45): 'said Jose Higuera applied to Governor Sola for a grant of the premises called Los Tularcitos... that under date of October 4, 1821, a decree was entered directing that said Higuera be put in possession of the land'; PDF p61 (228 ND p.47) 'Higuera went into possession of the premises soon after the concession was made by Sola in 1821'. Corroborated by the printed act of possession at PDF p431 (228 ND p.404): 'OCTOBER 23, 1821.-In compliance with the foregoing superior decree of the Superior Governor of the Province, Col. Don Pablo Vicente de Sola, ordering that possession of the place called Los Tularcitos be given to the invalid soldier, Jose Higuera... LUIS PERALTA'

governor.evidence: The granting governor is named repeatedly: PDF p431 (228 ND p.404) the decree is subscribed 'SOLA' and the act of possession recites 'the superior decree of the Superior Governor of the Province, Col. Don Pablo Vicente de Sola'; petition PDF p9 (228 ND p.4) 'Pablo Vicente de Sola Governor of the Province of California... granted to Jose Higuera (Father of these petitioners) a tract of land called De los Tularcitos'; Juan B. Alvarado's own deposition, PDF p14 (228 ND p.9), Q. 'whether Governor Sola and yourself were not acting as Governor of California respectively at the date of these grants. Answer. We were.' Register's 'a Spanish governor' is true in kind but unnamed

grantee.evidence: Register's grantee field holds the single word 'The' - a truncated fragment, not a name. The grantee is JOSE HIGUERA: PDF p431 (228 ND p.404) 'possession of the place called Los Tularcitos be given to the invalid soldier, Jose Higuera'; Board opinion PDF p59 (228 ND p.45) 'said Jose Higuera applied to Governor Sola for a grant of the premises called Los Tularcitos'; PDF p1 red label 'THE HEIRS OF JOSE HIGUERA CLAIMANT'. The claimants are his twelve children (Antonia, Fulgencio, Dolores, Valentin, Mariano, Josefa, Encarnacion, Florencio, Micaela, Rita, Refugio and Agustina de Higuera), PDF p9 (228 ND p.4)

corrections.governor: Pablo Vicente de Sola, Governor of the Province of California (decree 4 Oct 1821, possession 23 Oct 1821). The Sola grant was afterwards recognised and augmented by Governor Juan B. Alvarado's decree of concession of 14 February 1839 (PDF p60, 228 ND p.46)

notes: 337MB / 442 PDF images; stated 415 pages. Hoffman (year 1821, governor P. V. de Sola, grantee Jose Higuera, confirmed) agrees with the case file on every point; the register's 'The' and 'a Spanish governor' are the defective values. The bulk of this very large file is the 1857-61 SURVEY contest (Twitchell survey vs the official survey, Calaveras valley), which did not disturb the confirmation. NOTE for a re-reader: the register's year 1821 is right but the amended petition at 228 ND p.5 (PDF p10) appears to read '4th of October 1828', which cannot be correct - Sola left office in 1822 - and the Board's opinion, the act of possession and the original petition all read 1821.

notes: 112MB / 150 PDF images; stated 140 pages. Hoffman's grantee 'Marcelo Pio and Cristoval' agrees with the case file against the register - the dominant claimant-for-grantee error. Underlying expediente: petition of Marcelo, Pio and Cristobal at Monterey 21 March 1844, referred by Micheltorena/Jimeno to the First Alcalde of San Jose (Antonio Ma. Pico reported 2 May 1845); grant 19 May 1845; approved by the Departmental Assembly 3 June 1846 (PDF p38-39, 323 ND pp.32-33). Jacob D. Hoppe himself died during the case, leaving Lucy Hoppe and six children (PDF p47), which is why the register's patent_to reads 'the heirs of Jacob D. Hoppe'.

notes: 47MB / 47 PDF images; stated 39 pages. Hoffman's grantee 'Felipe' agrees with the case file against the register; his rancho column ('350 by 250 varas') also matches the grant's own description. Judicial possession given by Hugo Reid, acting Justice of the Peace, at San Gabriel 5 May 1845, witnesses Felipe Reid and Prospero (PDF p23, 58 SD p.17). The Board's opinion notes the original title paper was 'very much mutilated' but 'sufficiently authenticated and proved to establish its genuineness beyond all question' (PDF p24), and that no approval by the Departmental Assembly was ever proved.

notes: 134MB / 164 PDF images; stated 154 pages. Hoffman's 'governor: Gutierrez' agrees with the case file against the register's unnamed 'interim government'. Long prior history in the file that a register note could use: Portilla first petitioned Figueroa 20 Feb 1834; Figueroa's decree of concession is dated Monterey 30 July 1834 (PDF p20, 144 SD p.15, 'se declara al ciudadano Silvestre de la Portilla dueno en propiedad del terreno conocido con el nombre del Valle de San Jose'), but the Territorial Diputacion on 31 July 1834 RESERVED the expediente 'hasta que se verifique la secularizacion de las Misiones de la Alta California' (PDF p21-22, 144 SD pp.16-17), so the operative grant is Gutierrez's of 16 April 1836. The U.S. brief (PDF p163-164, 144 SD pp.149-151) argued Portilla abandoned the land and removed to Sonora, and that the same valley had been regranted to Jose Antonio Pico (Alvarado, 8 June 1840) and to J. J. Warner (Micheltorena, 28 Nov 1844, SD 218, confirmed) - the court rejected that argument. Survey plat transmitted to Washington for patent 20 Feb 1879 (PDF p148, 144 SD p.138), consistent with the register's 1880 patent date; no patent copy is in the file.

notes: 235MB / 317 PDF images; no typed page-count leaf, internal stamps run to at least 295. Hoffman-1862's 'rejected' is right as of 1862 but was SUPERSEDED: the Board rejected 17 Nov 1854, the District Court confirmed in 1863, and the U.S. appeal was dismissed 16 Jan 1865 - so the register's outcome is directionally right and only the patent step is unverified here. Grant was for 8 sitios de ganado mayor at Yokaya, north-west of Sonoma, 30 leagues distant, bounded south by Fernando Feliz and on the other sides 'con las tribus gentiles'; M. G. Vallejo certified the land vacant, Sonoma 8 April 1845 (PDF p13, 217 ND p.8). NOTE for a re-reader: a supplemental petition of 20 Dec 1852 set out a sale from Juarez to M. G. Vallejo and from Vallejo to Capt. E. Knight (deed 16 Aug 1852) and prayed that KNIGHT be substituted as claimant (index PDF p299, 217 ND p.277; abstract PDF p303, 217 ND p.291); the confirmation nevertheless ran to Juarez, and the register's blank patent_to should be checked against that chain in Phase C.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 342 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / ZAYANTA GRANT / ISAAC GRAHAM et al CLAIMANT'; PDF p5 transcript 'for the place named "Zayanta"'; petition PDF p9 (342 ND p.5) 'a certain tract of land called and known by the name of Zayanta near the Mission of Santa Cruz'. Printed briefs spell it 'Zayante' (PDF p384-385, 342 ND pp.368-369)

year.evidence: The grant is of 1841, not 1834. Printed brief of the settlers, PDF p385 (342 ND p.369): 'As we have seen, the grant was dated 22d April, 1841, and the measurement made and possession given in the same year. It appears from the espediente just mentioned, that in September, 1843, two years afterwards, Graham petitioned Governor Micheltorena, for a grant of the vacant land adjoining Zayante on the west'. Petition, PDF p9 (342 ND p.5): 'That on the 22d day of April 1841, Joseph L. Majors a Naturalized Citizen of Mexico solicited and obtained from the then Governor J. B. Alvarado a grant of a certain tract of land called and known by the name of Zayanta'. John Parrott's deposition, PDF p11 (342 ND p.7): 'the grant of land was made by Governor Alvarado on the 22d April 1841 in the name of Juan Jose Chrisostomo Major'. James W. Weeks's deposition, PDF p13 (342 ND p.9): 'a grant by said Alvarado to Don Juan Jose Chrisostomo Major dated April 22d 1841'

governor.evidence: Only ALVARADO is supported. PDF p9 (342 ND p.5) 'obtained from the then Governor J. B. Alvarado a grant'; PDF p11 and p13 (342 ND pp.7, 9), two witnesses identify the signatures of 'Juan B. Alvarado and Manl Jimeno' on the grant of 22 April 1841. Nothing in the pages read makes Figueroa the granting officer of this title. The register's compound 'Figueroa; Alvarado' most likely absorbs the SUPERSEDED earlier grants of the same tract, which the file records without naming a governor: J. L. Majors's own deposition, PDF p26 (342 ND p.22), 'The Rancho had been granted first to Joaquin Buelna and Bolcoff told me he had given Buelna Judicial possession and then it was granted to Francisco Mo[s] and Bolcoff gave Moss Judicial possession... and then it was granted to me'

grantee.evidence: The grantee of record is JOSEPH L. MAJORS, the grant running in his Mexican baptismal name. PDF p11 (342 ND p.7), John Parrott: 'the same man to whom the grant of land was made by Governor Alvarado on the 22d April 1841 in the name of Juan Jose Chrisostomo Major... he is the same man to whom the grant was originally made'. Majors's own deposition, PDF p23 (342 ND p.19): 'I am acquainted with said Rancho and it was granted to me for Isaac Graham and others[,] that is it was granted in my name because I was a Mexican Citizen and could hold the land and I held it for Graham and others who not being Citizens could not hold it in their own name. The other persons were William Ware, Peter Lassen, Frederick Heaple.' Graham and Ware are the CLAIMANTS, who took Majors's legal title by transfer of 22 May 1852 (petition, PDF p9 = 342 ND p.5: 'the said Joseph L. Majors has held the said Rancho of Zayanta in trust for your petitioners up to the 22d day of May last when he transferred to your petitioners all his right title and interest')

notes: 254MB / 387 PDF images. Typed leaf carries no total but warns 'Pp. 75-76 missing. Replaced with copies 6/18/85'; internal stamps run to at least 379. Hoffman-1862 (year 1841, grantee 'Juan Jose Crisostomo Mayor') agrees with the case file against the register on BOTH flagged fields. The register's '1834 / Figueroa' pairing is probably a conflation with the earlier, superseded grants of the same tract to Joaquin Buelna and then Francisco Mo[s] that Majors describes at 342 ND p.22 - the file gives no date or governor for those, so I have not asserted one. Judicial possession was given by Jose Bolcoff, First Alcalde of Santa Cruz, in 1841 (Bolcoff's deposition, PDF p19-22, 342 ND pp.15-18); Majors received the adjoining San Agustin rancho at the same time and took possession of both on the same day (PDF p384, 342 ND p.368).
